original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Characteristic 5 only, six sources, unchanged unsigned dirty connector. Decide whether the sixteen masks of weights 2 and 6 force S(16)=q_16+q_17 into {0,1,5,6,10}^6. The weight-6 windows and the weight-2 family do not. The conjunction of all sixteen on one word is left open. No kappa change.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one new connector operation. This package keeps the alphabet fixed and answers the first open question of open PR 7038: whether those sixteen masks determine the sum-33 centre. A new operation is not the missing step. The adjacent-centre question, the c=6 and c=7 remainders, and the merged DRAT certificate in PR 6216 are other questions.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the recursive-interface schedule. It does not change a supplier, a consumer, or kappa. It removes the separate weight-2 family and every all-ones window as transports onto a legal sum-33 centre, and it leaves the joint sixteen-mask fibre unresolved.
stop_rule: Stop when every admissible all-ones window is classified against S(16) and the fifteen weight-2 masks are realized at both centre polarities, or when a window that forces a legal centre appears.
evidence: Exhaustive finite census of 4095 all-ones type assignments: 2364 force an illegal centre (1573 because q_16 cannot contain a 0, by three human classes 845+721+7, and 791 by comparing every feasible vector with the 300 legal centres) and 1731 admit both polarities, with 5826 constructed floor words. The sorted staircase realizes all 15 weight-2 masks with an illegal centre; one explicit word realizes them with a legal centre. No allowed 6-tuple of sum 33 has weight 2 or 6. The joint sixteen-mask fibre is not decided.

open_questions.question: Does any satisfiable family made of the weight-6 mask and at least 14 of the weight-2 masks force S(16) into {0,1,5,6,10}^6?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The families decided in this package do not force a legal centre, and a forced legal centre is the input the PR 7038 freeze still lacks. Emptiness of all sixteen masks, as certified by PR 6216, does not select a centre.
open_questions.first_step: Take the fifteen weight-2 masks except (0,0,1,0,1,0), together with the all-ones mask, and either exhibit a floor word with illegal S(16) or prove that every realization has legal S(16).
open_questions.blocked_by: This census does not decide that 14-mask family. The weight identity still gives it no pair on s+t=33, and the PR 6216 certificate is not a derivation of the centre.
